title: HyCiM: A Hybrid Computing-in-Memory QUBO Solver for General Combinatorial Optimization Problems with Inequality Constraints
problem: Combinatorial optimization problems with inequality constraints require transformation into QUBO forms that introduce numerous auxiliary variables, resulting in substantially larger search spaces and increased hardware costs. Direct D-QUBO approaches become inefficient due to the exponential growth in problem size and computational complexity.
motivation: Efficient solvers for constrained combinatorial optimization are critical for enabling practical solutions to computationally challenging problems across various industrial and scientific applications.
method: HyCiM combines three working parts in a memory-based computing system. First, it directly encodes inequality constraints (conditions like 'x must be less than 10') into the optimization problem without adding extra dummy variables, keeping the problem smaller and cheaper to solve on hardware. Second, it uses ferroelectric FET transistors—transistors that store information using a ferroelectric material—in a computing-in-memory circuit to rapidly check whether solutions satisfy these constraints and automatically filter out invalid ones. Third, it applies iterative refinement using the same ferroelectric transistors to gradually improve solutions through simulated annealing, a method that explores many possibilities and progressively focuses on better ones.
key_novelty: This method directly transforms optimization problems with inequality constraints into QUBO form without requiring auxiliary variables, which substantially reduces the hardware cost of solving them.
contributions: Novel inequality-QUBO transformation method that directly handles constraints without auxiliary variables
FeFET-based CiM inequality filter circuit for accelerating constraint evaluation and pruning infeasible configurations
FeFET-based CiM annealer supporting iterative QUBO optimization via simulated annealing
Demonstrates 88.06-99.96% hardware area reduction and 98.54% average success rate compared to conventional D-QUBO

metrics.other: eliminates 2100-22536 infeasible configurations per problem instance

limitations: Limitations not discussed in the abstract.
